Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, some of which appear to have central cavitation or necrosis. In a patient presenting with chest pain and non-productive cough, this radiographic pattern of necrotizing nodules is highly characteristic of Necrotizing Sarcoid Granulomatosis (NSG), a rare variant of sarcoidosis that distinctively features vasculitis and necrosis unlike classic sarcoidosis.
